name: Margaret Carter

summary: Peggy Carter was born in June 1920 into a wealthy Richmond family regarded as Virginia royalty, and grew up alongside her brother Harrison. As a teenager she fell for a young Black man who ended the romance because of the racial climate of the time. That same night she was approached by Alexa Volkoff of the Daughters of Liberty, a secret society of women, who recruited her and became her handler. Trained into a sharp, resourceful operative, Peggy left for France once the Second World War broke out.

By 1943 she was a field agent in the French Resistance under the codename Agent 13. Working undercover in a cafe, she met a young soldier named Steve Rogers, and after Captain America walked in on her just after she had dealt with a room full of Nazi soldiers, the two began a lasting wartime romance. The Daughters had told her to stay close to Cap and keep him out of the wrong hands, but her feelings were genuine. She fought beside the Invaders, and in 1944 Nick Fury Sr. drafted her, Cap, Bucky and Dum Dum Dugan into a mission against Baron Zemo and the young Hydra.

In 1945 the two were sent on separate missions, and Peggy was captured by the Gestapo, tortured and lined up for a firing squad. As American troops stormed Paris she struggled with her captor, and a stray shell left her with amnesia, so she wandered away while Cap searched for her. She drifted around Europe for months until a family friend recognised her in Belgium and took her home, and news of Cap's apparent death sent her into a catatonic state. On the page she began as an unnamed woman from Cap's memories, glimpsed in Tales of Suspense #75 and shown in a full flashback in #77, and only received her name in Captain America #162 (1973).

comics.title: The woman Cap could not forget
comics.summary: Back in New York, Captain America spots a woman who reminds him of someone he loved during the war and is pulled into a S.H.I.E.L.D. operation to move a dangerous chemical through the city. Two issues later, a wartime documentary brings the memory back in full: a blonde Resistance leader he fought beside in occupied France, captured by the Nazis, and lost in the chaos of liberation when a shell blast took her memory and she slipped away unseen as cheering crowds carried Cap off. She has no name yet.

comics.title: Found at Lost Souls
comics.summary: Searching for a missing Sharon Carter, Cap and the Falcon find her family held by Doctor Faustus at the Lost Souls asylum in Connecticut, where the catatonic Peggy has been kept and questioned about Cap. Faustus stages a fake wartime Paris, with Sharon dressed in Peggy's old uniform, both to jolt Peggy's memory and to kill Cap. Peggy wakes with a scream, kills Faustus's assistant Dr. Wolfgang and is reunited with Cap. The story names her for the first time and presents her as Sharon's older sister; later continuity makes her Sharon's aunt.

comics.title: Moving on
comics.summary: Recovered, Peggy follows Cap to New York hoping to fight at his side as before, and when he refuses she joins S.H.I.E.L.D. instead. Paired with Gabe Jones, she goes undercover inside the Secret Empire and unmasks at the right moment to help Cap, the Falcon and the X-Men. Steve gently ends their romance, she falls for Gabe, and the Red Skull kidnaps the couple and tortures them for hours, defiant to the end, before claiming the Falcon as his own creation in front of them.

comics.title: Hate on the march
comics.summary: Peggy and Sharon are sent to infiltrate the National Force, a hate movement whose rallies whip crowds into violent agreement. After Sharon vanishes into the group, Peggy's car is bombed and she ends up in hospital, from which Doctor Faustus and William Burnside, the 1950s Captain America, abduct her as a hostage. Aboard Faustus's airship she learns that Steve Rogers and Captain America are the same man, breaks out of Faustus's grip and fights beside Cap until the craft goes down in New York harbour. Soon after, she is told Sharon has died, though years later it turns out Sharon was alive and working undercover.

comics.title: Running the comms room
comics.summary: Laid off when S.H.I.E.L.D. is dissolved, Peggy teams up with Cap, Fury, Dugan and Gabe on one last raid, and Cap then hires her to run the Avengers' communications. During Acts of Vengeance she helps defend Avengers Island as robots tear it apart and only just escapes before it sinks. The villain Mother Night later hypnotises the support staff, torments Peggy with visions of Sharon and turns her against her own party date, Gabe Jones, before the Avengers expose the plot.

comics.title: Stories at Larkmoore
comics.summary: When the Avengers are disbanded after their apparent deaths fighting Onslaught, the grief proves too much and Peggy's mind slips again. Living at the Larkmoore Clinic, she has lucid days full of war stories but struggles to recognise Sharon. She mentions visits from Steve Rogers, who was thought dead at the time; the visitor is really William Burnside, who sits with her and coaxes out every story she remembers.

comics.title: A funeral in Paris
comics.summary: A one-shot revisits Agent 13 in occupied France, from her first meeting with Steve to a rescue mission with her friend Anna. In the main Captain America series Peggy dies of old age and is buried in Paris, with a revived Steve, Sharon, Nick Fury Sr. and Dum Dum Dugan at the graveside. The ceremony is shattered when Codename: Bravo, a jealous former lover and ex-comrade from 1944, opens fire on the mourners to take revenge on Steve.

comics.title: Operation S.I.N.
comics.summary: Two flashback stories fill in Peggy's post-war years. In 1952 Howard Stark takes her to Moscow on a job that uncovers an alien beacon, a hidden Hydra bunker and a trapped extraterrestrial power, and she keeps insisting that nobody be killed for what they look like rather than what they have done. Another tale has Dum Dum Dugan invite her aboard a S.H.I.E.L.D. airship to vet a recruit, Lady Sif, only for Nick Fury to reveal that Peggy was the one being assessed; furious at the set-up, she turns him down and steals his flying car with Sif.

comics.title: Back from the grave
comics.summary: When the living Cosmic Cube Kobik rewrote reality, she accidentally brought Peggy back to life young again. Peggy quietly takes command of the Daughters of Liberty under the title of the Dryad. When Steve is framed for the murder of Thunderbolt Ross, she rallies the Daughters to help him and spends weeks tearing down the Foreigner's safe houses, while keeping her return hidden from Steve. When he starts looking for her, she has Agatha Harkness bring him in and tells him about the Daughters and her own past with them.

comics.title: War with the Power Elite
comics.summary: In Madripoor, Peggy, Misty Knight, Black Widow and Ross are captured by Sin and brought before the Red Skull and Alexa Lukin. Peggy slips her restraints, takes down Sin and Crossbones and chases Lukin to the roof, where a blast to the face sends her falling until the Falcon catches her. The fight against Lukin's Power Elite ends with Lukin shot dead during a kidnap attempt, and Peggy celebrates at the Carter family home with Steve, Sharon and Bucky before going back to work.

screen.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
screen.summary: A British agent of the Strategic Scientific Reserve, Peggy helps train the Project Rebirth candidates and sees the worth in the scrawny Steve Rogers before the serum transforms him. She urges him to be more than a USO mascot, flies with Howard Stark to drop him behind enemy lines to rescue the captured 107th, and joins the final assault on Hydra's base. As Steve brings the Valkyrie down in the Arctic, they arrange a dance date over the radio before the line goes dead.

screen.title: Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter
screen.summary: In 1946 Peggy is stuck with code-breaking and office work at the SSR, where her boss John Flynn keeps her off the hunt for the Zodiac serum. When a tip comes in one night, she goes after the Zodiac alone, fights through its guards and recovers the vial. Flynn is reprimanding her when Howard Stark calls to say she will help lead the new S.H.I.E.L.D.

screen.title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
screen.summary: Steve visits an elderly Peggy, who has Alzheimer's disease, at a Washington retirement home. She tells him the world has changed and that sometimes the best anyone can do is start over, then her memory slips and she greets him as if he had only just come back. The Smithsonian's Captain America exhibit also plays a 1953 interview in which she talks about him.

screen.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
screen.summary: Peggy appears in flashbacks in two second-season episodes, 'Shadows' and 'The Things We Bury'. In 1945 she leads an SSR raid with Dum Dum Dugan and Jim Morita on Werner Reinhardt's Hydra facility in Austria and seizes the alien Obelisk. Later she refuses Reinhardt's offer of a deal and sends him to prison for life.

screen.title: Agent Carter
screen.actor: Hayley Atwell (Gabriella Graves as young Peggy)
screen.summary: In 1946 New York, Peggy is sidelined at the SSR but secretly works with Howard Stark's butler Edwin Jarvis to clear Stark's name after his weapons are stolen, crossing paths with the Leviathan agents and the assassin Dottie Underwood; season one ends with her pouring the last vial of Steve's blood into the river. Season two (2016) sends her to Los Angeles, where she investigates Zero Matter and the actress-scientist Whitney Frost with Daniel Sousa, Jason Wilkes and Jarvis, and finally kisses Sousa. The series ran for 18 episodes from 2015 to 2016.

screen.title: Ant-Man
screen.summary: Cameo in the 1989 opening scene at S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Triskelion. Peggy sits with Howard Stark and Mitchell Carson as Hank Pym resigns in fury over attempts to copy his shrinking formula. After Pym storms out, she warns Carson not to make an enemy of a man they have already lied to.

screen.title: Avengers: Endgame
screen.summary: Peggy appears only as variants. At Camp Lehigh in 1970, Steve, hiding while he steals Pym Particles, watches through a window as she runs S.H.I.E.L.D. business in her office. After returning the Infinity Stones, Steve stays in the past to build a life with Peggy, and the film closes on the two of them dancing at home; the MCU Wiki lists the main-timeline Peggy only in a photo.

screen.title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
screen.summary: This is a variant: Captain Carter of Earth-838, a Peggy who took the super-soldier serum, led that world's Avengers and joined the Illuminati. She sits in judgement on the visiting Doctor Strange, explaining why her group executed their own Strange. When Wanda Maximoff storms the Illuminati headquarters, Captain Carter fights her and is killed with her own shield.

screen.summary: Marvel Studios returned Endgame to theaters on 25 September 2026, and co-director Anthony Russo told Marvel that the Encore plays one beat past the point where Steve's story ended with Peggy. unverified: Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter is dated 2013, not 2015: the MCU Wiki gives its release as 24 September 2013. The Agent Carter series (2015-2016, 18 episodes) is one entry under 2015, with season two (2016) covered in its summary.

Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015) is left out as a judgement call: Hayley Atwell is credited and filmed new material, but the MCU Wiki marks it '(vision)', because Peggy appears only inside the hallucination Wanda Maximoff gives Steve, not as the character herself. It can be added as a cameo if the site counts visions.
Captain America: Civil War (2016) is left out: the MCU Wiki credits Atwell there as a photo only. Peggy dies off-screen and Steve attends her funeral in London, where Sharon Carter gives the eulogy.

Also left out as photos, files, mentions or archive material, per the MCU Wiki: The Avengers (files in a deleted scene), Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 2 episode 2 and the Double Agent web series (photo), Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Slingshot and later Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. episodes (mentions), The Falcon and The Winter Soldier (indirect mention), She-Hulk: Attorney at Law (photo) and the Legends docuseries. What If...? (Captain Carter, voiced by Atwell) is animated and outside the live-action scope.

Avengers: Endgame (2019): the MCU Wiki lists the main-timeline Peggy only as a photo; the entry covers the Camp Lehigh (1970) and 'Steve Rogers' Married Life' variants, both played by Atwell. The wiki notes that the directors and writers disagree about whether Steve married an alternate Peggy or the one from his own past; the summary avoids taking a side.

Avengers: Endgame Encore (2026): the Marvel.com article confirms the extra beat with Steve and Peggy but does not describe it; the Loki detail comes only from the MCU Wiki's Encore plot summary. Nothing about what follows was researched.

Avengers: Doomsday appears in the MCU Wiki infobox for the 'Married Life' Peggy but is marked unreleased, so it is left out, along with a family detail on that page that is sourced to it. No plot details were researched.

Cameo flags are judgement calls where the role is a single scene or sequence (The Winter Soldier, Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. flashbacks, Ant-Man, Endgame, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, the Encore); the MCU Wiki does not tag any of them as cameos.

Creators: the Marvel Fandom character page lists Stan Lee, Jack Kirby and John Romita Sr. The Captain America stories in Tales of Suspense #75 and #77 credit Lee as writer and Kirby as penciller; Romita's part is not explained on the pages read. All three are kept to match the wiki.
First appearance: the wiki lists Tales of Suspense #75 as an obscured memory image, #77 as her first full appearance and Captain America #162 as the first time she is named.

The wiki gives conflicting accounts of how Peggy and Cap were separated in 1945 (Tales of Suspense #77, Captain America #162 and Operation: S.I.N. #1 differ); the origin follows the main account on the Earth-616 page.

Issue pages with no plot synopsis, so details rest on the Earth-616 character page and solicitations: Captain America #175, #351, Vol 5 #49, Vol 10 #9, #19, #25 and #30, Captain America and the First Thirteen #1 and Agent Carter: S.H.I.E.L.D. 50th Anniversary #1. The Captain America #179 synopsis does not mention Peggy; the break-up scene comes from the character page.
Young Peggy: the MCU Wiki infobox lists Gabriella Graves as young Peggy; the episode in which she appears (Agent Carter season 2 flashbacks) was not opened.
No non-MCU live-action Peggy was found: the Marvel Fandom disambiguation page lists only the Earth-199999 (MCU) version under live action.
